headline: Ai-Media CEO outlines four-pillar growth strategy centred on Lexy AI suite, with voice commercialisation expected in FY28-29 rather than FY27
reasoning: Tony Abrahams describes four elements of Ai-Media's growth strategy, all centred on the Lexy AI platform. The company's US broadcast business (55% of full-year revenue) is built around the EEG acquisition from 2021, which has held a near-monopoly on captioning encoding in the US since 1980 and defines the gold standard for RFPs. Churn risk is mitigated by zero churn among top 20 customers over five years. Lexy Voice is being piloted with customers such as the City of Sacramento and Taiwan but is expected to take until FY28 or FY29 to reach meaningful commercialisation, as voice technology still lags translation quality — particularly around emotional fidelity for live sport. The CEO flagged an upcoming AGM investor day with detailed product announcements as a near-term catalyst for investor understanding.
quote: Look, I don't necessarily think FY 27 is going to be the year where. Voice itself. Right. Like, like hits it out of the park. It took Lexy text four years to really reach that commercialization process. Where 18 months in on voice. It's probably going to be an FY 28 or an FY 29 kick with voice, because the voice technology is still lagging the translation technology a bit. We can't quite get that same level of emotion that someone who wants to watch the World Cup in a native language is going to be able to replicate. But the Taiwan example and the City of Sacramento example are great examples where you already have product market fit in more kind of niche situations.
episode_title: The Lexi lift: AI-Media’s shift to AI-native growth

headline: Ai-Media CEO outlines deliberate revenue mix shift to AI-native technology platform as legacy services wind down
reasoning: Tony Abrahams explains that FY26 results reflected a deliberate investment phase: the company upgraded its core fleet of captioning encoders for the first time in ten years, resolving 37 security flaws and building a next-generation AI-native encoder platform. About $3 million annualised in investment is now in the rearview mirror and the company will begin shipping the new encoders in H1 FY27. Legacy human-in-the-loop services were deliberately shut down in December, ending revenue decline from that segment. Lexi Text SaaS revenue grew 42% year-on-year to $34.1 million and total revenue is expected to grow. The hardware decline of $6.4 million is attributed to customers waiting for the new encoder rather than demand erosion.
quote: I think the highlight of the full year results was really the second half, because in the first half we deliberately invested in getting all of our products up to the AI native environment, and principally that was with our core fleet of captioning encoders. And these encoders sit at the point of broadcast. And this was the first upgrade that we had done in ten years. So we resolved 37 fundamental security flaws across that architecture. And so we've got brand new AI. Native encoder platform. We will begin shipping those this half. Um, but all of the investment in getting that done, about 3 million annualized, uh, is in the rearview mirror now, which is good.
episode_title: The Lexi lift: AI-Media’s shift to AI-native growth

headline: Ai-Media's Lexi Direct software platform embeds captioning natively inside third-party broadcast ecosystems, broadening distribution beyond proprietary hardware
reasoning: Abrahams describes Lexi Direct as a software encoding platform that turns third-party hardware into an encoder, allowing Lexi to operate inside another vendor's broadcast walled garden. As an example, Ai-Media is now natively embedded within Grass Valley's AMP playout system, enabling Grass Valley customers to purchase Lexi services via Grass Valley tokens. This move is designed to take Lexi beyond hardware-only broadcast delivery into software, education, and government markets, significantly expanding the total addressable market.
quote: The other thing that we've built, which is even more fundamental, is a software encoding platform called Lexi Direct, which effectively turns somebody else's hardware into an encoder and allows Lexi to sit inside somebody else's broadcast walled garden. So, for example, Grass Valley have an AMP playout system. We are now natively embedded within Grass Valley, so if someone is a customer of Grass Valley, they can then select to pay for Lexi via their Grass Valley tokens. So it's about really getting, um, Lexi out of just a hardware delivered broadcast infrastructure, um, into hardware and software and then taking it outside of broadcast, putting it into education and putting it into government markets.
episode_title: The Lexi lift: AI-Media’s shift to AI-native growth

headline: Ai-Media CEO addresses 60%-plus share price decline, arguing market is underestimating successful transition and wallet-share expansion opportunity with North American broadcasters
reasoning: Abrahams acknowledges the share price has fallen over 60% in the past year and roughly halved in recent weeks. He believes the market is conflating general AI uncertainty with company-specific risk and is not fully appreciating the conversion of legacy services to Lexi nor the growth potential from new AI-delivered products. North American broadcast represents 55% of total revenue and those customers are spending more each year. New products including Lexi Voice (live voice translation tested at the World Cup), Lexi for recorded media, and Lexi Audio Description represent additional wallet-share opportunities with existing customers.
quote: Look I think there's a lot of uncertainty around AI who's going to win in AI. What companies are going to benefit from that. And I think what people want to see is that we're successfully converting not just our legacy human services business across to Lexi, but we're also able to then grow that. Lexi sweet of services with the existing broadcasters that we've got now, 55% of our total revenue comes from just one sector, which is North American broadcast. And those North American broadcasters are spending more and more with us every year. So what we're trying to do is we're trying to increase the range of AI delivered services that we offer these broadcasters by adding in Lexi voice, which is live voice translation into your workflow. We tested that with the World Cup. English into Spanish. Spanish into English worked really well.
episode_title: The Lexi lift: AI-Media’s shift to AI-native growth
